items.title: The tangent data (8.1)–(8.9): $T(X, \mathbf X)$ and its structure maps

book.label: §8.1, (8.1)–(8.9), pp. 357–359 (2017 pp. 257–258)
book.statement: The tangent of the ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$ is the pair $T(X, \mathbf X) = (TX, T\mathbf X)$ (8.1), to be equipped with the structure of an ep-groupoid with object M-polyfold $TX$ and morphism M-polyfold $T\mathbf X$. A tangent vector $(\varphi, h) \in T_\varphi\mathbf X$ is viewed as a morphism $(\varphi, h) : Ts(\varphi)(h) \to Tt(\varphi)(h)$ (8.2), so that $s_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, h) = Ts(\varphi)(h)$ and $t_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, h) = Tt(\varphi)(h)$ (8.3). If $s_{T\mathbf X}(\psi, k) = Ts(\psi)(k) = Tt(\varphi)(h) = t_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, h)$ (8.4), which implies $s(\psi) = t(\varphi)$, the multiplication is $(\psi, k) \circ (\varphi, h) = (\psi \circ \varphi, Ts(\psi \circ \varphi)^{-1}(Ts(\varphi)(h))) \in T_{\varphi \circ \psi}\mathbf X$ (8.5), where $k = Ts(\psi)^{-1}(Tt(\varphi)(h))$; with the projection $\mathbf p : T\mathbf X \to \mathbf X^1$, shorter, $k \circ h = Ts(\mathbf p(k) \circ \mathbf p(h))^{-1}Ts(\mathbf p(h))(h)$ (8.6). items.title: Theorem 8.1.12 (2017: 8.3): the functor $T : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}$

book.label: §8.1, Theorem 8.1.12 (2017: 8.3), p. 366 (2017 p. 266)

items.title: §8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1): the morphisms over a fibre and the isomorphism classes

book.label: §8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1), before Lemma 8.6.1 (2017: 8.9), p. 397 (2017 p. 286)
book.statement: For a proper covering functor $F : Y \to X$ and $x \in X$, let $X(x)$ be the full subcategory on $x$, with the morphisms $G_x$, and $Y(x)$ the full subcategory on the finite set $F^{-1}(x)$, with the morphisms $\mathrm{mor}(F^{-1}(x))$. By Definition 8.5.1 (3) (2017: 8.8), $\mathrm{mor}(F^{-1}(x)) \to G_x \times F^{-1}(x)$, $\varphi \mapsto (F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, is a bijection, so $\#\mathrm{mor}(F^{-1}(x)) = \#G_x \cdot \#F^{-1}(x)$. $F^{-1}(x) = \Theta_1 \cup \dots \cup \Theta_q$ is the decomposition into isomorphism classes, and for $y, y' \in \Theta_j$ the isotropy groups $G_y$, $G_{y'}$ are isomorphic.

lean.statement: `IsProperCovering.bijective_fibredMap`, `IsProperCovering.existsUnique_lift`: $\varphi \mapsto (F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$ is a bijection; `IsProperCovering.morOnFiberEquiv`: $\mathrm{mor}(F^{-1}(x)) \simeq G_x \times F^{-1}(x)$; `IsProperCovering.ncard_morOn_fiber`: $\#\mathrm{mor}(F^{-1}(x)) = \#G_x \cdot \#F^{-1}(x)$, a finite set (`IsProperCovering.finite_morOn_fiber`). `fiberClass x c` $= \Theta_c = F^{-1}(x) \cap \pi^{-1}(c)$ for $c \in |Y|$, `fiberIndex x` the $c$ that occur, `fiberClasses x` the classes; they cover $F^{-1}(x)$ and are disjoint (`iUnion_fiberClass`, `pairwiseDisjoint_fiberClass`), and the isotropy groups in one class have the same order (`nat_card_isotropy_eq_of_mem_fiberClass`).

items.title: Lemma 8.6.1 (2017: 8.9): $\#G_x \cdot \#\Theta_j$ and $\#G_x = \#G_{y_0} \cdot \#\Theta_j$

book.label: §8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1), Lemma 8.6.1 (2017: 8.9) and its proof, pp. 396–398 (2017 pp. 286–287)
book.statement: For every $j = 1, \dots, q$: $\#G_x \cdot \#\Theta_j = \#\{\psi \in \mathrm{mor}(F^{-1}(x)) \mid s(\psi), t(\psi) \in \Theta_j\}$. Moreover, for every $j$ and $y_0 \in \Theta_j$, $\#\{\psi \in \mathrm{mor}(F^{-1}(x)) \mid s(\psi), t(\psi) \in \Theta_j\} = \#G_{y_0} \cdot (\#\Theta_j)^2$ and $\#G_x = \#G_{y_0} \cdot \#\Theta_j$. items.title: Lemma 8.6.2 (2017: 8.10): the isomorphism classes over isomorphic objects

book.label: §8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1), Lemma 8.6.2 (2017: 8.10) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 287
book.statement: Given a proper covering functor $F : Y \to X$ and isomorphic $x$, $x'$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between the isomorphism classes of $F^{-1}(x)$ and of $F^{-1}(x')$: if $F^{-1}(x) = \bigsqcup_{j=1}^q \Theta_j$ is the decomposition into isomorphism classes, there is a decomposition $F^{-1}(x') = \bigsqcup_{j=1}^q \Theta'_j$ such that, if $y \in F^{-1}(x)$ and $y' \in F^{-1}(x')$ are connected by an isomorphism, there is a uniquely determined $j$ with $y \in \Theta_j$ and $y' \in \Theta'_j$. (Before the lemma: the objects of $F^{-1}(x')$ reachable by a morphism from $y \in F^{-1}(x)$ are mutually isomorphic, and so are those reachable from the class of $y$.)

lean.statement: `IsProperCovering.exists_isomorphic_of_isomorphic`: every $y \in F^{-1}(x)$ is isomorphic to some $y' \in F^{-1}(x')$. `IsProperCovering.fiberIndex_eq` and `IsProperCovering.lemma_8_10`: $F^{-1}(x)$ and $F^{-1}(x')$ have the same index set in $|Y|$, and isomorphic $y \in F^{-1}(x)$, $y' \in F^{-1}(x')$ lie in $\Theta_c$ and $\Theta'_c$ for exactly one $c$. `IsProperCovering.lemma_8_10_equiv`: a bijection between the sets of classes, matching isomorphic elements.

diff: The correspondence is "the same index $c \in |Y|$"; as a bijection of the sets of classes it is `lemma_8_10_equiv` (Findings, Chapter 8, items 71, 73).

items.title: Lemma 8.6.3 (2017: 8.11): $\#F^{-1}(x) = \#F^{-1}(x')$ for isomorphic $x$, $x'$

book.label: §8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1), Lemma 8.6.3 (2017: 8.11) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 287
book.statement: Given a proper covering functor $F : Y \to X$ and isomorphic $x$, $x'$, with the decompositions of $F^{-1}(x)$ and $F^{-1}(x')$ of Lemma 8.6.2 (2017: 8.10): $\#\Theta_j = \#\Theta'_j$ for every $j = 1, \dots, q$; in particular $\#F^{-1}(x) = \sum_j \#\Theta_j = \sum_j \#\Theta'_j = \#F^{-1}(x')$. (Before the lemma: for $y_0 \in \Theta_j$ and $y_0' \in \Theta'_j$, $\#G_{y_0} = \#G_{y_0'}$, and $\#G_x = \#G_{x'}$; with "the third claim of Lemma 8.10", $\#\Theta_j = \#G_x/\#G_{y_0} = \#G_{x'}/\#G_{y_0'} = \#\Theta'_j$.)

lean.statement: `IsProperCovering.lemma_8_11`: $\#\Theta_c = \#\Theta'_c$ for every $c \in |Y|$, and $\#F^{-1}(x) = \#F^{-1}(x')$. `IsProperCovering.ncard_fiber_eq_sum`: $\#F^{-1}(x) = \sum_c \#\Theta_c$; `IsProperCovering.ncard_fiber_eq_of_isomorphic`.

diff: As in the text (Findings, Chapter 8, item 73).
"The third claim of Lemma 8.10" for that of Lemma 8.6.1 (2017: 8.9), and the summation index $i$ with summands $\#\Theta_j$ (possible misprints).

items.title: Proposition 8.6.4 (2017: 8.4): the number of sheets is constant on components of $|X|$

book.label: §8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1), Proposition 8.6.4 (2017: 8.4) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 288
book.statement: The structure of isomorphism classes of $F^{-1}(x)$ stays the same if $x$ is perturbed, which follows from the definition of a proper covering functor; together with Lemma 8.6.3 (2017: 8.11) this gives: let $F : Y \to X$ be an sc-smooth proper covering functor. Then for every connected component $c$ of the orbit space $|X|$ there is a constant $k_c$ such that $\#F^{-1}(x) = k_c$ whenever $\pi(x) \in c$. In other words, viewing $\mathbb N = \{1, 2, \dots\}$ as an ep-groupoid with the identities as the morphisms, the map $X \to \mathbb N$, $x \mapsto \#F^{-1}(x)$, is an sc-smooth functor.

lean.statement: `IsProperCovering.proposition_8_4`: for every connected component $c$ of $|X|$ there is $k$ with $\#F^{-1}(x) = k$ for all $x$ with $\pi(x) \in c$. The proof: $\#F^{-1}(x) \ge 1$ (`IsProperCovering.one_le_ncard_fiber`), locally constant on $X$ (`IsProperCovering.eventually_ncard_fiber_eq`, `IsProperCovering.isLocallyConstant_ncard_fiber`) and constant on isomorphism classes (Lemma 8.6.3 (2017: 8.11)), hence a locally constant function on $|X|$ (`IsProperCovering.fiberCardOrbit`, `IsProperCovering.isLocallyConstant_fiberCardOrbit`). `IsProperCovering.fiberCardFunctor`: $x \mapsto \#F^{-1}(x)$ is an ep-functor into the trivial ep-groupoid (`EpGroupoid.trivial`) of the discrete M-polyfold $\mathbb N$ (`discretePolyfold`).

diff: $\mathbb N$ is Lean's, with $0$, as the trivial ep-groupoid of the discrete M-polyfold; the values are $\ge 1$. Only the local constancy of $\#F^{-1}(x)$ is used, not "the structure of isomorphism classes stays the same" (Findings, Chapter 8, item 74).

items.title: §8.6.2 (2017 §8.5.2): the structure of strong bundle coverings

book.label: §8.6.2 (2017 §8.5.2), 2017 pp. 288–289
book.statement: For a proper strong bundle covering functor $A$ as in Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10), with $Q \circ A = F \circ P$: a strong bundle $P : W \to Y$ over an ep-groupoid comes with $\mu_Y$, associating with a morphism $\varphi : y \to y'$ a topological linear isomorphism $\mu_Y(\varphi) : P^{-1}(y) \to P^{-1}(y')$, a morphism $w \to w'$ being a pair $(\varphi, w) : w \to \mu_Y(\varphi)(w)$; the same holds for $Q : V \to X$. On morphisms $A(\varphi, w) = (F(\varphi), A_{s(\varphi)}(w))$, where $A_y : P^{-1}(y) \to Q^{-1}(F(y))$ is the topological linear isomorphism induced by $A$, and $t(A(\varphi, w)) = A(t(\varphi, w))$ gives $\mu_X(F(\varphi)) \circ A_{s(\varphi)} = A_{t(\varphi)} \circ \mu_Y(\varphi)$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf Y$. With $\mathrm{Ban}$ the category of Banach spaces and topological linear isomorphisms, $\mu_Y : Y \to \mathrm{Ban}$ and $\mu_X : X \to \mathrm{Ban}$ are functors, and $y \mapsto A_y$ is a natural transformation $\mu_Y \to \mu_X \circ F$.

lean.statement: `IsProperStrongBundleCovering.mor_val`: $A(\varphi, w) = (F(\varphi), A(w))$; `IsProperStrongBundleCovering.fiberEquiv y`: $A_y : W_y \to V_{F(y)}$, a topological linear isomorphism; `IsStrongBundleFunctor.μ_comm`: $\mu_X(F(\varphi), A(w)) = A(\mu_Y(\varphi, w))$; `section_8_5_2`: $\mu_X(F(\varphi)) \circ A_{s(\varphi)} = A_{t(\varphi)} \circ \mu_Y(\varphi)$ on $W_{s(\varphi)}$, for every morphism $\varphi$ of $Y$.

diff: The natural transformation $\mu_Y \to \mu_X \circ F$ is stated as its naturality identity; of Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10) only the strong bundle functor part and the fibre isomorphisms $A_y$ enter (Findings, Chapter 8, item 75).

notFormalized.title: Definitions 8.2.1, 8.2.2 (2017: 8.2, 8.3): sc-differential forms on ep-groupoids and the sc-de Rham complex
notFormalized.label: §8.2, Definitions 8.2.1 and 8.2.2 (2017: 8.2 and 8.3), pp. 372–375 (2017 pp. 268–270)
notFormalized.book: Definition 8.2.1 (2017: 8.2): an sc-differential $k$-form on the ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$ is an sc-smooth map $\omega : \oplus^k TX \to \mathbb R$ on the Whitney sum of the tangent of the object M-polyfold, linear in each argument and skew-symmetric, with $(T\varphi)^*\omega_y = \omega_x$ for every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ in $\mathbf X_1$; $\Omega^k_{ep}(X)$ is the vector space of these forms. A form on $X^i$ is a form on $X^{i+1}$, and $\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}(X)$ is the direct limit of the directed system $\Omega^*_{ep}(X^i) \to \Omega^*_{ep}(X^k)$, $i \le k$. The exterior derivative is $d[\omega] := [d\omega]$, with $d\omega$ compatible with morphisms and $d \circ d = 0$. Definition 8.2.2 (2017: 8.3): $(\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}(X), d)$ is the sc-de Rham complex of the ep-groupoid $X$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** It needs the Whitney sums $\oplus^k TX$ as M-polyfolds, the linear structure of $T_xX$ (gap G.7), linear maps $T\varphi$ (gap G.70), the M-polyfolds $X^i$ for $i \ge 2$ (gap G.6) and the sc-differential forms, the Lie bracket and the exterior derivative of Part I's §4.4 (gaps G.37–G.39), none of which is formalized. Nothing else in Chapter 8 depends on it. Definition 8.2.1 (2017: 8.2) writes $T_yY$ for $T_yX$ (possible misprint) (Findings, Chapter 8, item 110).
